reasons: The finding is claimed compliant, and no redline or counterparty comment was proposed — consistent with expectations for a compliant finding.

The cited paragraphs (Section 5 fees/revenue share and Section 6 use restrictions) contain no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right exercisable by Kubient against the Customer, and no remote/direct system-access language, so no walk-away trigger exists.

Absence of any Vendor audit right is more favourable to us than the preferred position; inserting audit limits would create a vendor right that does not exist, so declining to redline is the correct minimal-edit outcome.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is expected here — it simply reflects that no audit clause exists to constrain, not a substantive gap.

The rationale accurately notes, without over-flagging, that AP may separately want its own audit right over Kubient's Impression measurement; that is a customer-favourable addition outside this rule's scope.
